tweet.text:
Recipe is @MiaAI_lab DeepSeek V4.1 Flash EXL3 2.9bpw on vLLM TP=2 across two DGX Sparks, thinking off, DSpark k=3 draft, SHA 8530568.

https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks

https://huggingface.co/Mia-AiLab/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-EXL3-2.9bpw

Full write-up with every table (empty-context lanes, concurrency ladder to 128, needle, decode-after-fill, jobs at depth, warm session):

https://github.com/yume-arasaki/yume_benchmarks/blob/main/reports/2026-09-14-dsv41-flash-exl3-two-sparks.md

Gotchas from our own boot, so you can skip the failures I already paid for:

The Engram tables are not in the EXL3 repo. You need shards 47 and 48 from deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, about 95 GiB each, and you point at them with --hf-overrides engram_table_dir. Skip this and the load dies with no useful message.

Do not force an fp8 KV cache dtype from an older DeepSeek recipe. This checkpoint wants its native V4.1 FP4 KV at about 890 bytes per token. vLLM picks fp8_ds_mla on its own if you leave the flag off.

DSpark is in-checkpoint, so there is no external draft model to download. You enable it with --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3}'.

Thinking defaults on at the base card. For a clean non-reasoning smoke, disable it per request with enable_thinking=false in the chat template kwargs. The whole grid ran that way.

Weight sync across the two nodes is NFS. Budget the disk and the first load time.

Depth labels in my results are actual usage.prompt_tokens, not pack targets. The filler overshoots about 2.1x on this tokenizer, so a 256k target is really 548k prompt tokens.

Decode numbers are completion tokens over time after the first content token. Wall includes prefill and is always slower, never compare the two.

Concurrency sweep in full (prose-600, MAX_NUM_SEQS=2): C1 29.08, C2 43.46, C4 30.43, then it drifts down to 23.8 by C128. Past two clients system throughput plateaus and queue pressure slowly eats it.

The 4.9 joules per generated token is measured across a full turn, prefill plus decode, on the 35k-prompt agent lane. That metric is workload-specific. The same measure on a deep-context decode lane reads in the hundreds, because most of the energy went into prefill.
